campaign_name: DUMBO District — facade, surface and planting evidence
purpose: The district corpus that proved this pipeline, and the reason the human is in the loop at all: the automatic screen could not tell an office interior from a street view, so 537 photographs were reviewed by a person instead. Those decisions are preserved verbatim and reloaded by this sheet. The category vocabulary is unchanged from scripts/build_photo_corpus.py REVIEW_CATEGORIES, which remains the authority for how a decision becomes an aspect in the survey; this config exists so the review SHEET can come from digital-3d-shared-contracts rather than being a fork.

categories.label: Building facade
categories.help: A building exterior you could read a material or colour from.

categories.label: Street surface
categories.help: Cobblestone, paving, kerbs, the ground underfoot.

categories.label: Street furniture
categories.help: Benches, lamps, railings, bollards, bike racks.

categories.label: Landmark
categories.help: Jane's Carousel, the Archway, a named thing rather than a generic building.

categories.label: Bridge (another module owns this)
categories.help: Brooklyn or Manhattan Bridge. Kept and credited, never used to derive district geometry.

categories.label: Historic
categories.help: Archival. Describes a DUMBO that may no longer exist.

categories.label: Context only
categories.help: Area designation, maps, signage, wayfinding. Not geometry.

categories.label: Water's edge
categories.help: Rocks, riprap, the beach, where the land stops and the river starts.

categories.label: Grass and lawn
categories.help: Park lawns, planted beds, grass meeting paving.

categories.label: Railings and fences
categories.help: The promenade guard rail, park fences, handrails.

temporal_note: A 'renewed' subject is replaced on a maintenance cycle, so a photograph of it describes only the day it was taken. A 'stable' subject is substantially original fabric, so an archival frame is still evidence about it.
